A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Matching relocated material and renumbered figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E report original synthetic and image-benchmark experiments, including permutation errors, concept and label accuracy, impurity scores, and execution times.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and adds an experiment testing alignment with mixtures of causal variables.

M1.justification: The CRL-to-concept pipeline, linear and kernelized Group Lasso estimators, permutation matching, and binary logistic variant are retained. The mixture experiment changes evaluation inputs without introducing a new estimator.

E1.justification: The four datasets remain unchanged. Appendix E.1 adds a distinct Toy Dataset scenario with partially mixed causal representations, simulating imperfect disentanglement by the preceding CRL method.

E2.justification: The continuous Toy comparisons remove the curves labelled 'lasso', retaining 'group', Pearson, and Spearman comparisons; this is visible in Figure 2 and the corresponding appendix plots. Neural-network alignment, CBM, CEM, and HardCBM comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new mixture experiment varies mixing strength, dimensions 30 and 50, and regularization, with n=1250 and zero correlation under both specification settings. It introduces paired mean permutation error. Previously documented experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 and new Figures 20–21 add a controlled robustness analysis of imperfect disentanglement, testing individual-variable versus pair-level recovery as mixing increases. Earlier correlation-shift and feature-sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: The existing 10-seed percentile plots and 10- or 50-seed mean-and-standard-deviation tables retain their reporting practices. The new ablation also uses 10 random repetitions; no increased run count for existing experiments or new statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds mixture-error results and removes Toy Lasso result series. Retained curves also change: Figure 2's wellspecified d=100 correlation-baseline errors shift from approximately 0.48–0.49 to 0.42, and execution-time curves are revised, including v2 Figure 7 versus v3 Figure 8. Tables 1 and 8–12 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and proofs in Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–C are unchanged. The added mixture experiment and discussion do not establish new theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same scope: sample-efficient concept alignment, finite-sample linear guarantees, asymptotic kernel guarantees, and favorable concept accuracy and impurity. The revised introduction makes previously reported binary evaluations and beyond-assumption performance more explicit.

C2.justification: Sections 3 and 7 expand the rationale for continuous-variable theory, clarify that block identifiability permits block-level alignment, and explain that the alignment itself does not use causal semantics. v3 also interprets the mixture experiment and discusses a possible logistic Group Lasso extension for discrete concepts.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 specifies random pairing and the mixture construction M'_j=(1-a)Mi+aMj for the new experiment. Figure 3 explains which alignment and training stages are timed. Existing code-access information, hardware, architectures, and training details in Appendix D are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kong et al. (2024) to qualify the discussion of discrete-variable identifiability and connects the already cited Meier et al. (2008) to a possible theoretical extension. The principal related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted additions expand the introduction, framework explanation, and discussion. Section 7 becomes 'Conclusions and Discussion'; algorithm cross-references and publication/funding text are updated. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds mixture Figures 20–21 and a main-text runtime Figure 3 presenting an analysis already covered in v2's appendix. Existing plots receive revised legends, markers, ticks, and spacing, including removal of Lasso series. Tables are retained, with layout and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: The controlled mixture experiment and clearer continuous-variable and block-alignment limitations modestly improve the paper's account of applicability. The gain is qualified by removal of the Lasso comparison and robustness wording broader than some settings in Figure 21 support. The central method, theoretical guarantees, and benchmark tables remain unchanged.
